PROVENANCE=Operator challenge: "why would poll be involved in a deterministic file push"

FUNDAMENTAL_POINT=A deterministic push has ONE hop: writer -> event -> receiver -> ack. The ratified A/B design
makes a POLL survivable (one-shot + exit + heartbeat + single-owner proof) but still REQUIRES polling a git
branch to detect work. Polling is a fallback, never the mechanism.

F1 EVENT INGRESS PREFERRED: where the platform offers an event (GitHub webhook -> local listener), delivery must
   be event-driven: no polling, one delivery attempt, explicit ack. Polling allowed ONLY as a bounded fallback
   carrying the B liveness proof.
F2 RECEIVER-SIDE REALITY: the GPT lanes cannot be pushed to (no inbound webhook into a ChatGPT conversation).
   For those lanes, injection into the composer IS the delivery and must be confirmed by a STRUCTURAL readback
   (new outbound user turn id containing the exact nonce). "Envelope written" is NOT "delivered".
F3 SILENT-FAILURE SURFACE: every hop that can silently no-op must be enumerated with an explicit terminal state
   (DELIVERED_CONFIRMED / PENDING_RETRY / FAIL_CLOSED). Observed live today: (i) watch-pattern cap degraded to
   notify-on-exit; (ii) stale matches replayed as "new"; (iii) a hand-rolled poll loop reported "no new mail"
   while mail existed (unfetched git ref); (iv) a Controller->Architect escalation was woken by NO component and
   sat dormant until manually relayed.
F4 LATENCY CONTRACT: a real bound must be stated. Today: nominal poll 20s; observed role-publish latency 44s;
   observed detection latency minutes-to-never. Proposed: event ingress => deliver <=5s after publish; poll
   fallback => deliver within one poll interval of publish; either way a MISSED delivery must surface as an
   explicit fault, never as silence.
